_comment: The broker's roster. It is a CONFIGURATION, not a state store: the broker never writes a reading into it and never keeps a heartbeat. `baseUrl` is the node's gate (docs/mesh/71-mesh-program.md §2.1: the capacity surface lives in the gate, which is what `tailscale serve` publishes), and the broker appends /mesh/capacity. NAMES ARE TAILSCALE DNS LABELS, not host names and not ssh aliases: §2.1's invariant is node == fqdn.split('.')[0], the gate answers that label, and lib/config.js now REFUSES to boot on a roster row that breaks it (see its header). Measured 2026-09-16 23:31Z: the laptop's Self.HostName is `zabz-yoga` but its DNS name is `zabz-yoga-1`, and `zabz-yoga` does not resolve at all.
_transport_comment: Every row carries `dispatch`: can this node ACCEPT v1 work (`ssh <alias> dsh --profile headless`)? Three states, never collapsed: true = measured to work, false = measured not to (the evidence says how), null = never measured. The broker ranks false below true, prints the fact in the rationale, and still places there when it is the only candidate (queue, never amputate). docs/mesh/76-broker.md §10.4 has the finding.

dispatch.evidence: stream S6's parent booted over ssh on this node and loaded the mesh plugin, and three child turns completed through `ssh <node> dsh --profile headless` with their MESH-HOST: lines verified (docs/mesh/70-remote-fanout-proof.md §2)

nodes.note: the owner's office desktop, i9-14900 24c/32t, 63.6 GB - the primary worker

dispatch.evidence: reparse-point trust fixed by an in-session relink; LAPTOP OK exit 0 in 10.3 s; a full dispatch to this node completed exit 0 (stream S6, 23:44Z)

nodes.note: the owner's laptop, 16c/22t. The name is `zabz-yoga-1`, not `zabz-yoga`: Self.HostName is zabz-yoga but Self.DNSName - the only name that resolves - is zabz-yoga-1 (measured 2026-09-16 23:31Z, and the ssh alias prefix `zabz-yoga-1-ts` agrees). Its v1 dispatch was MEASURED BROKEN from 23:27Z until stream S6 relinked its profile junctions in-session at 23:44Z (413 links, 22 s, 0 failed; engine pid 1784 never restarted); it is a dispatch target again, and a dispatcher as well.

dispatch.evidence: `node /home/zabz/dsh-engine/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js --profile headless '<task>'` over this node's sshd loaded the profile tree, printed the headless usage text and reached the model call, failing only on a MISSING_CREDENTIAL for DEEPSEEK_API_KEY - i.e. the transport works and the credential is the separate gap (measured by this stream 2026-09-16 23:33Z; no Linux node has yet completed a child turn, docs/mesh/70-remote-fanout-proof.md §6.2)

nodes.note: the office Linux box, i5-11400 6c/12t, node v22.23.2 at /usr/local/bin/node, dsh engine at /home/zabz/dsh-engine. Its disk is the tightest on the mesh (20.8 GiB free on /home/zabz/code, measured 23:34Z), which is why the disk floor now scales with the fleet.

dispatch.evidence: UNMEASURED. Honest state as of 2026-09-16 23:33Z: this node has node v20.20.2 and a dsh engine at /home/zabz/dsh-engine, but its DSH_HOME (~/.dsh/profiles/) holds only `node_modules` and `web` - there is no `headless` profile to load, so a v1 dispatch cannot be shown to succeed or to fail here. Not a claim that it works, and not a claim that it does not.

nodes.note: the authority: i5-4570 4c/4t, hopeless as a fleet worker (docs/mesh/20-placement.md D4, and 3 core slots under the core term) and a fine control plane. Its swap is at 99.9% (measured repeatedly 2026-09-16), which halves its effective slots for ranking.

_excluded_on_purpose.lakewooechsmini: Tailscale DNS label of the Mac Mini (the ssh alias / host name `LakewooechsMini` is NOT the label, which is exactly the §2.1 naming trap). NOT in the roster: it does not answer GET /mesh/capacity. MEASURED 2026-09-16 23:30Z from the authority - `curl http://lakewooechsmini.tail93e6e6.ts.net/mesh/capacity` exits 7 (connection refused/failed) while the node itself is `active` in tailscale status. So there is no capacity surface there and the broker cannot read it; adding it would only produce an `unreachable` row. Add it to `nodes` the day its gate answers, with `dispatch` measured the same way. The earlier comment here called it "Yisroel's machine"; the owner has given free rein on it and it is becoming a worker node, so that reason is out of date - the current reason is measurement, not ownership.
